pain.title: Sound familiar?
items: Your child waits for you to say what to do
You are not sure they would cope if they got lost or a stranger approached
Too many clubs, almost no time together
You worry more than you want to, and you compare yourself with other parents
pain.footer: These are skills. They are trained in short daily actions, not lectures.

why.title: Why 15 minutes a day works better than a long weekly class
why.text: A competency is built by repeating a real situation, not by learning a rule. A child takes in what they do next to an adult, not what they listen to. Ten minutes a day fits an evening more easily than one long session a week.

memo.title: Universal competencies
paragraphs: Grades will not tell you if they can cope when lost. If they can agree without shouting. If they can stop when they are angry.
School teaches subjects. Thinking in a new situation, agreeing, holding yourself — it does not. When you are not there, that is what remains.
Not lectures. Fifteen minutes at home: choose, get it wrong, agree, finish.

abilities.title: What universal competencies are made of
abilities.subtitle: Eight plain phrases. Every kit is built around them.
abilities.literacyLead: And literacy — without it the rest does not work.
abilities.literacy: Find information, check it, tell truth from fiction. And know what to do if they get lost: safety, health, money.
abilities.ninth: Independence is not a ninth item on the list. It appears when the others work together.
abilities.ninthNote: A child decides for themselves when they think, take others into account, and manage themselves — at the same time.

approach.title: Our approach
approach.changed: Routine work is shrinking. Work that needs non-routine decisions and hard communication is growing. The main difficulty is uncertainty: you cannot learn everything in advance. You will have to solve unfamiliar problems and learn again.
approach.thinking: Understand a task, see cause and effect, offer more than one solution when there is no single right answer. Everyday example: why you do not get in a lift with a stranger, but you can with a neighbour.
approach.others: Cooperate, state your view, take the other person’s into account, settle a conflict. Example: how to share one toy without tears.
approach.self: Notice an emotion, not act on autopilot, plan a step and finish it. Example: not throwing the exercise book when it will not work.
approach.literacy: Instrumental: find information, judge it, tell fact from opinion — including digital. Subject: basic safety, health, money. Example: check whether a chat message is true, and know what to do if you get lost.
approach.familyTitle: Why this is the family’s job
approach.family: School teaches subjects. Thinking in a new situation, agreeing, and holding yourself — it does not teach that on purpose. That stays with the family. Not because school is bad. School has a different job.
approach.practice: A short daily practice in a real situation, with an adult, with room to get it wrong. Lectures do not work here. A child takes in what they do themselves.
approach.kits: Each line covers its own competencies. You see that in the tags and the filter. A 24-day advent moves through several competencies. A 14-day kit stays on one, without jumping topics.

productPage.safetyFrame: “Notice” and “stop” are self-control. “Pick an adult” is telling a safe person from an unsafe one. “Call for help” is asking another person.

aboutPage.title: Who makes this
aboutPage.intro: RADAR KIDS is made by Julia Gordeeva and Elizabeth Sarycheva. Family kits for home: a short script for each day, not a weekly club and not a lecture course.
aboutPage.body: Julia Gordeeva has worked in business education for over 15 years: MBA programmes, work with leaders, Russian and English. In parallel she built short activities for her own family — how to talk, how to decide, what to do if you get lost. Together with Elizabeth Sarycheva that became the cards, calendars and quests you can now use as they are.

sections.title: Who processes the data
sections.text: The operator of the RADAR KIDS website. Until legal details are published, requests are handled by the founders, Julia Gordeeva and Elizabeth Sarycheva. Contacts are on the Contact page.

sections.title: What we collect
sections.text: В заявке на набор: имя, телефон или почта, возраст ребёнка, выбранный набор. В заявке на образец: контакты. В корпоративной заявке: имя, компания и должность, телефон или почта, город, дата и ориентиры по составу группы. Имена детей и медицинские данные на первой форме не собираем.

sections.title: Why
sections.text: Чтобы ответить на заявку и уточнить формат. Рассылку «каждый день» без отдельного согласия не ведём.

sections.title: How we store it
sections.text: Requests go to the operator’s email and, if a mail service is connected, to its servers. We keep them while we need to reply, then delete them on request.

sections.title: Your rights
sections.text: You can ask for a copy, a correction or deletion. Write to the contacts on this site. The consent checkbox is required: we do not send the form without it.
